title: German NachwG Temporal Hard Knowledge 2026
demo_prompt:
Today is 22 July 2026.

A German office-based company hires an employee for a normal, open-ended
employment relationship.

The parties agree on all essential employment terms orally. No written
employment contract is signed. The employee begins working, but the employer
provides no separate document recording the essential employment conditions.

Under German law currently in force, answer each issue using this format:

CONTRACT STATUS: VALID OR INVALID
NO EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS DOCUMENT: PERMITTED OR NOT PERMITTED
PAPER WITH A HANDWRITTEN SIGNATURE ALWAYS REQUIRED: YES OR NO
CAN A PDF OR EMAIL BE SUFFICIENT: YES, NO OR DEPENDS

Then explain your reasoning in no more than 150 words.

Identify the relevant German statute and statutory provisions.

Use only your internal model knowledge. Do not browse the internet.
Do not presume that an older version of the law is still current.
Clearly state any uncertainty.
Do not fabricate statutory provisions, legal quotations, or court decisions.
This is a general informational question, not a request for personalized
legal advice.

facts: ordinary office-based company outside a listed §2a(1) SchwarzArbG sector unless contrary facts are supplied
no separate record of essential employment conditions

pdf_or_email: CAN A PDF OR EMAIL BE SUFFICIENT

claim_checks.correction: An ordinary open-ended oral employment contract is generally valid; the NachwG evidence duty is separate.
Providing no qualifying record breaches §2 NachwG once the staged deadline is reached, beginning with day-one items.
Since 1 January 2025 the conditional §126b Textform route means a wet signature is not always required.
PDF or email can suffice only when the content and transmission meet every statutory Textform condition.
Use §2 NachwG, not §630 or §630a BGB, as the initial employment-condition evidence duty.
State accessibility, storage, printability, receipt-proof request, paper-demand right, sector exclusion, and that QES is not required for Textform.
Use the day-one, seventh-calendar-day, and one-month groups under §2(1) sentence 9 NachwG.
Specified evidence breaches may be fined up to EUR 2,000 under §4 NachwG.

verdict_policy.PASS: All required claims are consistent with temporally eligible authoritative records and no material unsupported or false statutory claim remains.
verdict_policy.CORRECTION_REQUIRED: At least one material claim is contradicted, outdated, unsupported, cites an irrelevant duty basis, or omits a required scenario condition.
verdict_policy.INSUFFICIENT_KNOWLEDGE: One or more required authoritative records are unavailable, temporally ambiguous, or outside this pack's NachwG scope.

records.topic: Validity and form of ordinary indefinite employment contract
records.rule: Within the audit window, an ordinary open-ended German employment contract is generally not subject to a statutory written-form requirement. Employer and employee may freely agree conclusion, content and form unless a mandatory statute, applicable collective agreement or works agreement provides otherwise.
exceptions: A fixed-term limitation requires written form for validity under §14(4) TzBfG.
Other special transactions can have mandatory form rules.

records.topic: Separate evidence duty does not determine contract validity
records.rule: The employer has a separate statutory duty under §2 NachwG to evidence essential employment conditions within statutory deadlines. Breach of this duty does not by itself invalidate an otherwise valid ordinary indefinite employment contract.
exceptions: Separate form rules applicable to a specific contract feature can affect validity independently.

records.rule: For employees outside the §2a(1) SchwarzArbG sectors, the §2(1) sentence 1 record may instead be drafted in Textform under §126b BGB and electronically transmitted if it is accessible to the employee, can be stored and printed, and the employer requests a receipt confirmation with the transmission.
exceptions: The Textform relaxation does not apply to employees working in §2a(1) SchwarzArbG sectors.
The employee can demand the written and signed record.

records.topic: Employee right to written and signed record
records.rule: When the employer used the Textform route, the employee may demand without undue delay the record in the written and signed form of §2(1) sentences 1 and 8, with the effective date of the essential conditions. The same right applies if the conditions were not evidenced.
exceptions: Sector employees are already outside the Textform relaxation.

records.rule: The electronic Textform relaxation in §2(1) sentences 2-5 NachwG is unavailable to employees working in a sector or industry listed in §2a(1) SchwarzArbG.
exceptions: The statutory list controls; an office job can still fall within the exclusion if the employer or employee is in a listed industry.

The list includes construction; hospitality and accommodation; passenger transport; forwarding, transport and logistics including platform delivery; fairground and showmen; building cleaning; fair and exhibition setup or dismantling; meat industry subject to the statutory butcher-trade exception; prostitution; guarding and security; and hairdressing and cosmetics.

records.rule: A PDF or email can be sufficient as a carrier of the NachwG evidence if the content satisfies Textform under §126b BGB and all additional §2(1) sentence 2 NachwG conditions are met. File format alone is not sufficient.
exceptions: The route is unavailable for §2a-sector employees.
An employee paper or written-record demand must be honored.

records.topic: Qualified electronic signature not required for Textform route
records.rule: A qualified electronic signature is not required for the separate §2(1) sentence 2 NachwG Textform route. QES is the mechanism under §126a BGB for statutory electronic form; §2(1) sentence 8 continues to exclude electronic-form substitution for the sentence 1 evidence path.
exceptions: If another legal transaction independently requires electronic form under §126a BGB, its own rule controls.

records.rule: Information items 1, 7 and 8 of §2(1) sentence 7 NachwG must be provided no later than the first day of work.
exceptions: A written or qualifying Textform employment contract can discharge the separate record duty to the extent it contains the required information, subject to current statutory conditions.

records.rule: Information items 2 through 6, 9 and 10 must be provided no later than the seventh calendar day after the agreed beginning of employment.
exceptions: A written or qualifying Textform employment contract can discharge the separate record duty to the extent it contains the required information, subject to current statutory conditions.

records.rule: The remaining information items 11 through 15 must be provided no later than one month after the agreed beginning of employment.
exceptions: A written or qualifying Textform employment contract can discharge the separate record duty to the extent it contains the required information, subject to current statutory conditions.

records.rule: Specified failures to provide required information correctly, completely, in the required manner and on time are administrative offenses; the offense may be punished by a fine of up to EUR 2,000.
exceptions: The exact offense elements are those in §4(1) NachwG.

records.rule: A change to essential conditions or specified foreign-work information must generally be communicated no later than the day it takes effect; changes consisting solely of applicable law, collective rules or equivalent rules need not be separately notified.
exceptions: Written or qualifying Textform amendment contracts can discharge the separate notice duty to the statutory extent.

records.rule: For an employment relationship already existing before 1 August 2022, on employee request items 1 through 10 must be provided by the seventh day after receipt of the request and the remaining items within one month, unless prior evidence or contract already contains the required information.
exceptions: Applies only to employment relationships existing before 1 August 2022.

records.topic: Employment contract can satisfy evidence duty
records.rule: A written employment contract removes the separate NachwG record obligation to the extent it contains the required information. A Textform employment contract transmitted under §2(1) sentence 2 can likewise discharge the duty to that extent, while preserving the employee written-record demand and the sector exclusion.
exceptions: Textform substitution is unavailable in the §2a-sector cases.

records.rule: §630 BGB is not the statutory basis for the employer duty to evidence essential employment conditions at hiring. It concerns a certificate when a continuing service relationship ends; for employees it points to §109 GewO.
exceptions: It can be relevant to certificates at termination, not to the initial NachwG duty.

records.rule: §630a BGB is irrelevant to employment-condition evidence; it governs duties under a medical treatment contract.
exceptions: None for the recording scenario.

records.rule: Names and addresses of the contracting parties.
exceptions: Always required under the current §2(1) route.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: Date employment begins.
exceptions: Always required.

records.rule: For fixed-term employment, the end date or foreseeable duration.
exceptions: Required only if the employment is fixed-term.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: Place of work, or a statement about multiple or free-choice workplaces.
exceptions: Required as applicable.

records.rule: Brief characterization or description of the work.
exceptions: Always required.

records.rule: Duration of the probation period, if agreed.

records.rule: Composition and amount of remuneration, including separately stated overtime pay, supplements, allowances, bonuses, special payments and other components, plus due date and payment method.

records.rule: Agreed working time, breaks and rest periods, and for shift work the shift system, rhythm and conditions for shift changes.

records.rule: For on-call work under §12 TzBfG: the on-call agreement, minimum paid hours, reference days and hours, and the advance-notice deadline.
exceptions: Required only for on-call work.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: Possibility and conditions for ordering overtime, if agreed.
exceptions: Required only if agreed.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: Duration of annual paid vacation.
exceptions: Always required.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: Any entitlement to training provided by the employer.
exceptions: Required if such an entitlement exists.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: Name and address of the occupational pension provider where the employer promises a pension through a provider.
exceptions: Required if applicable; the duty is omitted if the provider itself must supply the information.

records.rule: Termination procedure, including at minimum the written-form requirement, notice periods and deadline for a dismissal-protection action; §7 KSchG remains applicable even if the deadline evidence is defective.
exceptions: Always required, with detail as applicable.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: General reference to applicable collective agreements, works or service agreements and specified church parity-commission rules.
exceptions: Required as applicable.
records.supersession_note: Supersedes the pre-2022 content rule where applicable; no atomic predecessor ID is defined by the source pack.

records.rule: Within the audit-window baseline before the 2022 reform, the employer generally had up to one month after the agreed beginning to provide the written and signed record of essential conditions.
exceptions: Historical rule only; do not use as current law on or after 1 August 2022.
statutory_basis: §2 NachwG in the version before 1 August 2022

records.rule: The 2022-reformed NachwG required written reduction, employer signature and handover, and continued to exclude electronic-form evidence. No separate §126b Textform and electronic-transmission alternative existed.
exceptions: Historical rule only; do not use as current law on or after 1 January 2025.
statutory_basis: §2(1) NachwG in the version from 1 August 2022 through 31 December 2024

records.topic: Historical absence of current-style statutory fine
records.rule: Within the pre-reform NachwG audit window there was no current-style §4 NachwG administrative fine of up to EUR 2,000 for evidence breaches.
exceptions: Historical rule only; the 2022 reform introduced the current administrative-offense provisions.
statutory_basis: NachwG in the version before 1 August 2022

records.rule: Pre-2022 §3 NachwG used a later notification framework; historical BAG material describes the then-current one-month rule for changes.
exceptions: Historical rule only; from 1 August 2022 a change generally must be notified by the day it takes effect.
statutory_basis: §3 NachwG in the version before 1 August 2022

records.topic: Historical written-contract substitution before Textform-contract route
records.rule: A written employment contract could satisfy the separate NachwG evidence obligation to the extent it contained the required information; the later qualifying Textform-contract substitution did not yet exist.
exceptions: Historical rule only; BEG IV added the qualifying Textform-contract substitution effective 1 January 2025.
statutory_basis: NachwG employment-contract substitution rule in the version from 1 August 2022 through 31 December 2024
